summary: The main article describes an electrochemical method for the selective hydrocarboxylation of acrylamides with CO2. It includes 8 figures and 1 table detailing optimization, substrate scope for alpha and beta carboxylation, control experiments, and mechanistic pathways.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Hydrocarboxylation of electron-deficient alkenes with CO2. (a) Hydrocarboxylation reactions of acrylates with CO2. (b) Previous hydrocarboxylation of acrylamides with CO2. (c) This work: Electrochemical selective hydrocarboxylation of acrylamides with CO2.
items.description: This figure provides context by comparing previous methods for hydrocarboxylation of acrylates and acrylamides with the current electrochemical selective approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions. [a]
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of anodes, electrolytes, solvents, and temperatures to optimize the yields for both alpha and beta carboxylation products.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Scope of the β -carboxylation reaction. [a] Reaction conditions: undivided cell, Mg plate anode (10 mm × 20 mm × 0.5 mm), C plate cathode (10 mm × 20 mm × 1.0 mm), 1 (0.2 mmol), TBAC (0.2 mmol), CO2 (1 atm), DMF (3.0 mL), 8 mA, 3.5-5 h. [b] 4 mA, 6 h.
items.description: This figure displays the chemical structures and yields of various acrylamide substrates converted to beta-carboxylation products.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Scope of the α -carboxylation reaction. Reaction conditions: undivided cell, Mg plate anode (10 mm × 20 mm × 0.5 mm), C plate cathode (10 mm × 20 mm × 1.0 mm), 1 (0.1 mmol), TEAClO4 (0.2 mmol), CO2 1 atm), CH3CN (3.0 mL), 6 mA, 3.5-5 h.
items.description: This figure illustrates the substrate scope for the alpha-selective hydrocarboxylation of acrylamides.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: The other scope of the β -carboxylation reaction. Reaction conditions: undivided cell, Mg plate anode (10 mm × 20 mm × 0.5 mm), C plate cathode (10 mm × 20 mm × 1.0 mm), 4 (0.1 mmol), TEAClO4 (0.2 mmol), CO2 (1 atm), CH3CN (3.0 mL), 4 mA, 6 h.
items.description: This figure shows the beta-carboxylation products obtained when using indole-substituted acrylamides.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Control experiments. (a) Large-scale reactions. (b) Radical trap experiments. (c) Deuterium labeling experiments. (d) Proton source exploration experiments.
items.description: This figure details various experimental tests used to probe the reaction mechanism, including radical trapping and deuterium labeling.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Calculated reduction potentials and reaction diagrams for the carboxylation of 1a . 1a is reduced (top) and CO2 is reduced (bottom).
items.description: This figure presents DFT calculation results comparing the reduction pathways of the substrate versus carbon dioxide.

items.heading: Fig. 8
items.caption: Plausible mechanism. The reaction pathways of α -carboxylation (top) and β -carboxylation (bottom).
items.description: This scheme outlines the proposed chemical pathways for the regioselective formation of alpha and beta products.
